summary: Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and sinology. He served on the faculty at both the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union from circa 1986 to 2008.

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, founding the Archiv für Religionswissenschaft. He studied at Mainz, Berlin, Heidelberg under Kuno Fischer, and Freiburg. He was a professor of philosophy at Freiburg (1885-1893) and held a chair at Fribourg (1894-1898).

Edmund Leach worked in religious studies and related fields. Educated at Cambridge and the London School of Economics, he lectured at LSE (~1947-1953) and served as Professor at Cambridge (1953-1978), Provost of King's College (1966-1979), and RAI President (1971-1975).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in Buddhist studies and psychology. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Böhmer was a linguist who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1845-1851). He later held academic posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1859-1872) and the University of Strasbourg (~1872-1879).

Eduard Erkes was a sinologist who studied at Leipzig University under August Conrady (~1909-1913), whom he later succeeded. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1917-1958) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1950-1958).

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Freiburg, and Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He held posts at Kiel (1913), Frankfurt (1914), and served as Professor at Göttingen (1917-1937).

Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed an inaugural dissertation at Leipzig University (~1871-1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern from circa 1886 to 1908.

Eduard Röer worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Königsberg, Jena, and under Herbart and Bopp. He held a postdoctorate at Berlin (1833) and worked for the East India Company, the Asiatic Society, and Bibliotheca Indica.

Eduard Sachau specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Brockhaus, Fleischer, and Nöldeke. He held professorial posts at Vienna (1869) and Berlin (1876-1920), directing the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Eduard Schwyzer was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1902-1927), the University of Bonn (~1927-1932), and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932-1943).

Linguist Eduard Sievers studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Curtius, Leskien, and Zarncke. He founded Beiträge zur Geschichte der deutschen Sprache und Literatur and held professorships at Jena (1871-1883), Tübingen (1883-1887), Halle (1887-1892), and Leipzig (1892-1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Edvard Westermarck was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881-1889) and later held posts at the London School of Economics (~1907-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918-1932).

Edward Albert Gait was an administrator and scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1880-1882) and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914, serving as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charterhouse and Oxford. He served as Professor of Hindustani and Telugu at East India Company College (1845) and worked at the Foreign Office (~1860-1863).

Edward Byles Cowell specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson, became Principal of Sanskrit College (1858-1864), and served as Professor at the University of Cambridge (1867-1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr. worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. Educated at Yale and Harvard (PhD 1959), he was an assistant professor at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and president of the American Institute of Indian Studies (1972-1986).

Edward Capps studied at Illinois College, Yale University, Humboldt University of Berlin, Munich, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held academic posts at Illinois College (1887-1888), Yale University (1890-1907), and Princeton University (1907-1936).
